claims.text: encoding default values into the code logic prevents altering defaults without rewriting logic
claims.quote: Please don't encode default values in how the code is written. This makes it impossible to change the default values without rewriting the code logic.
claims.status_note: author changed parameter handling to use Arg<bool>
claims.status_by_quote: Thanks for the suggestion, yep it is cleaner. Now should be as easy as changing the default in the arg definition.

claims.text: floating-point types cannot represent decimal monetary amounts accurately, causing imprecise or wrong values in RPC output
claims.quote: this is wrong, you can't use `double` to denote monetary amounts. `double` is a floating point type, which can not represent decimal values accurately.
claims.status_note: author switched to fixed-point integer arithmetic and string formatting

claims.text: drags an RPC-only dependency (UniValue) into a widely included policy header
claims.quote: This drags an RPC‑only dependency (UniValue) into a widely included policy header.
claims.status_note: author moved the helper to core_write.cpp and core_io.h
claims.status_by_quote: Moved the function into `core_write.cpp` and `core_io.h` similar to function `ValueFromAmount`.

claims.text: introduces an RPC-to-RPC include and constructs an entire object with locking just to read two values
claims.quote: This line constructs a full object (with locking) only to reuse two values. It also adds a new include `<rpc/mempool.h>` into `rpc/net.cpp`, creating an RPC‑RPC dependency.
claims.status_note: author removed the dependency and locking in a rebase
claims.status_by_quote: True! ... I think I just misunderstood and the intention was to maybe remove them in the future

claims.text: changing the default unit format in the future would be a massive API break leaving downstream software readings orders of magnitude off
claims.quote: It seems extremely dangerous to ever change the default... no matter how much notice is given, it's a massive api break that would cause software to suddenly be several orders of magnitude off.
claims.status_note: author confirmed the PR is backwards compatible and that they would not push to change the default
claims.status_by_quote: I don't think the default will ever be changed. I left the door open to it in some comments, but I would not push for it

claims.text: estimaterawfee produces mixed-unit responses by converting the top-level feerate but leaving pass/fail bucket ranges in sat/kvB
claims.quote: `estimaterawfee` is converting only the top-level feerate when `satvB=true`, while `pass/fail.startrange` and `endrange` remained in the `sat/kvB` units.
claims.status_note: author converted bucket ranges in estimaterawfee and w0xlt verified

claims.text: simplify negative feerate handling by using unsigned cast before division
claims.quote: Would it make sense, or is there a reason not to simplify this by stripping the negative sign right at the start using static_cast<uint64_t>?
claims.status_note: author declined, preferring current conditional structure for readability
claims.status_by_quote: I rather keep as is for now, unless someone finds a better reason for it. I think is more readable

claims.text: provide a release note if changing positional RPC argument order
claims.quote: In particular changing positional RPC arguments porbably warrants a release note (if we do have to break that ordering).

claims.text: update PR description if it is no longer a PoC
claims.quote: I think the description needs updating too, if this is no longer a PoC.

claims.text: use self.(Maybe)Arg<bool> instead of manual argument parsing
claims.status_by_quote: btw: I used `self.Arg<bool>`, I think it makes more sense, `self.MaybeArg<bool>` is defined for optional params with no defaults.

claims.text: add a global configuration option to toggle the default feerate representation
claims.quote: There could be a global option to toggle the default, to improve the UX.
claims.status_note: author explained it could be dangerous for external programs like Lightning nodes
claims.status_by_quote: That would be great for a `bitcoin-cli` user, but probably fatal for other programs that rely on the Bitcoin Core RPC.

claims.text: the new feerate formatting logic does not handle negative feerates correctly
claims.quote: I don't think it handles negative feerates correctly. Generally, it is best to write unit or fuzz tests for newly written code.

claims.text: do the last six lines of the test duplicate assertions instead of testing negative sat/vB cases?
claims.quote: Do the last six lines duplicate three assertions ? You probably intended to add negative sat/vB cases.
claims.status_note: author confirmed and fixed in subsequent commit

claims.text: changing the default unit format in the future would be a massive API break leaving downstream software readings orders of magnitude off
claims.quote: It seems extremely dangerous to ever change the default... no matter how much notice is given, it's a massive api break that would cause software to suddenly be several orders of magnitude off.
claims.status_note: author replied agreeing not to change the default
claims.status_by_quote: I don't think the default will ever be changed. I left the door open to it in some comments, but I would not push for it

claims.text: add a separate field to each result like feerate_satvb controlled by a global config option rather than changing existing fields
claims.quote: A different approach could be to add another field to each result, like "feerate_satvb". A global config option like `-feeraterepresentation" could determine which results are returned
claims.status_by_quote: how would you do it for rpc arguments though? Unless you force to use named arguments I think it can still lead to errors.

claims.text: use snake_case sat_vb instead of satvb per developer naming guidelines
claims.quote: Would it be better to use `sat_vb` or `satvb` for these? (Sorry if this has already been discussed above.) Per the developer notes
claims.status_note: author changed parameter naming to sat_vb
